title: Large Bricks and Join-irreducible Torsionfree Classes

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The arXiv listing (arXiv:2405.05635) and ADS abstract for this paper explicitly contain the author's comment: 'Found a gap in the proof of Proposition 3.9.' This is the paper's main result — that every join-irreducible torsionfree class is cogenerated by a single brick. The author has publicly acknowledged the proof is incomplete. Web search confirms this comment appears verbatim in the arXiv metadata for this paper. The proof relies on a chain of lemmas (3.6, 3.7, 3.8); Lemma 3.7 in particular has an underjustified step (claiming a non-zero map F→S is a monomorphism 'by simplicity of F' without establishing that F is simple in the heart of the t-structure).

The proof of Lemma 3.7 establishes an epimorphism F→S in the heart H (where S is a torsion simple and F is lim→ f-simple), then claims this map 'must be a monomorphism, by simplicity of F.' However, F's simplicity in the heart H has not been established — F is only known to be lim→ f-simple in Λ-Mod. The relationship between lim→ f-simplicity and simplicity in the t-structure heart is not argued. This gap is likely related to the acknowledged gap in Proposition 3.9, which depends on this lemma.

References [1], [2], and [3] are cited in the body of the paper but are entirely missing from the bibliography. [1] is cited as 'the survey [1] for the basic notions of silting/cosilting theory' (line 83). [2] is cited as the source of Lemma 2.3 and Theorem 3.6 (lines 105, 118). [3] is cited as the source of Theorem 1.0.5 by Barnard, Carroll, and Zhu (line 13). The bibliography only contains entries [4] through [11].

Both the proof of Corollary 2.6 and the forward direction of Proposition 2.9 rely on the inference that for an f-simple object B, membership in cogen(X) for a class X implies membership in X itself. Specifically: 'B ∈ cogen(v ∪ w) that is B ∈ v or B ∈ w' (Cor 2.6 proof) and similar inferences in Prop 2.9. The fact that cogen(v ∪ w) consists of submodules of finite coproducts of objects from v ∪ w does not directly imply that an f-simple submodule must belong to v or to w — this step requires additional justification, possibly involving properties of the lattice of torsionfree classes.

summary: The paper 'Large Bricks and Join-irreducible Torsionfree Classes' by Francesco Sentieri (arXiv:2405.05635) attempts to prove that every join-irreducible torsionfree class in the category of finitely generated modules over an artinian ring is cogenerated by a single brick. Verification found 4 issues, including one critical finding: the author has publicly acknowledged (in the arXiv metadata) a gap in the proof of Proposition 3.9, which is the paper's main result. The proof of Lemma 3.7 (a key dependency of Proposition 3.9) contains an underjustified step where simplicity in the heart of a t-structure is asserted without being properly established. Additionally, references [1], [2], and [3] are cited in the body but missing from the bibliography. The cross-section consistency check found no internal contradictions in the paper's logical structure. Verdict: NEEDS_CORRECTION — the acknowledged gap in the main result's proof requires resolution before the paper's central claim can be considered established.

cross_section_consistency.findings: The paper is internally consistent. The abstract correctly summarizes the main result (Proposition 3.9). The distinction between completely join-irreducible and merely join-irreducible torsionfree classes is maintained consistently throughout. The logical flow from definitions (monobricks, f-simples, directed posets) through intermediate results (Proposition 2.9, Corollaries 2.6, 2.10, 2.11) to the main result (Proposition 3.9) is coherent. No contradictions were found between sections.
